correctness.rationale: The proof derives a uniform bivariate normal orthant asymptotic from Gaussian integration and exponential-moment domination, then controls the inverse-normal quantile shift when log(u/v)=O(log log(1/u)). This yields the exact ratio constant and a strictly decreasing Gaussian-to-Marshall-Olkin ratio along each vertical section. Limit comparisons guarantee exactly one crossing and its asymptotic location. Boundaries and fixed-rho quantification are explicit; 63 independent numerical integration checks support but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The exact 1/log(1/u) transition and unique crossing resolve a natural comparison of two canonical asymptotically independent models calibrated to the same diagonal exponent. They determine a sharp tail-order reversal with unequal marginal thresholds and demonstrate the failure of global local ordering despite fixed-ray ranking. This is a structural probabilistic boundary, not an arbitrary constant or routine recomputation.
